first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A wedding planning company that helps foreign couples get married in Portugal, palaces in Sintra down to cliffs in the Algarve. The second line about starting the legal process a month ahead caught me straight away, and 'Some couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home' told me they know about the paperwork. Nothing up top says anything about small groups or what it costs though.

attention_map.quote: Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
attention_map.why: Documents are my big worry, so seeing the legal timeline in the second line kept me reading. The headline 'from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff' feels grand, not small.
This is the first place I looked for a guest range, but it is just a dropdown saying 'Choose'. I can't see if 'under 10' or '30 or fewer' is even an option.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue (Pena, Monserrate, Queluz, Douro, Algarve)
attention_map.quote: Queluz offers its upper gardens and Throne Room for events
attention_map.why: Pretty palaces, but a Throne Room is not what I picture for me and my parents. Lots of scrolling before anything about small groups.

Every region lists its airport, which is exactly what I want, something simple and close to a flight. I also caught 'an elopement, a small wedding or a three-day weekend' in the intro, the first sign small is fine.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra
attention_map.why: Useful honesty, but it is palace detail I don't need.

attention_map.section: Pick the Setting for Your Ceremony
attention_map.quote: Catholic marriage is one of three recognised forms and is still registered through the civil registry.
attention_map.why: This answers my Catholic question clearly. 'In the city. Lisbon City Council... offer public municipal spaces for civil ceremonies' also sounds like a simple small option.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill.
attention_map.why: This is exactly the trap for a small group. Good that they flag it, but it also tells me there may be a minimum and they still don't tell me what it is.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Marrying Legally
attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part.
attention_map.why: This is the bit I came for. Numbered steps, documents listed, translation rules, my passport section, and named official sources. 'Gather your documents. ID, a birth certificate, and a certificate of capacity to marry' is clear enough that I'm not scared of it anymore.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things... We talk you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: No number at all, not even a starting point or a minimum. This is exactly the 'you have to call us to find out' thing I hate.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: A welcome dinner the night before... A late party... Sunday brunch before everyone heads home
attention_map.why: This is a big three-day production. 'There is no set Portugal package' answers my package question with a no. I just want a ceremony and a nice lunch with close family.

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Some quintas have rooms for your closest guests
attention_map.why: 'Closest guests' is nice, but the section is still about filling an estate.

attention_map.section: Celebrate More Than a Wedding (honeymoon, anniversary, proposal, vow renewal, birthday)
Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: Your advisor talks you through your options: regions, venues, the legal route for your passport and what drives cost.
attention_map.why: One person helping with everything is what I said I need. But 'talks you through' is not the same as 'we sort the documents for you'.

attention_map.quote: Elopements and small weddings are welcome.
attention_map.why: Finally said plainly, but it is right at the bottom next to the form. If this was at the top I'd have relaxed much sooner. The form is easy and phone is optional.

attention_map.quote: Yes. Witnesses are optional in a Portuguese civil ceremony, so the two of you can marry with no guests at all
attention_map.why: Question 9 is basically my question. It makes a small or tiny wedding feel normal here. Question 3 confirms Catholic again.

attention_map.section: Trending now / Explore More of Europe
attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity weddings feel off for what I'm planning. I stopped here.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: Small is welcome: 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome.' and FAQ 9 'Can You Have a Small Wedding or Elopement in Portugal? Yes.' But no package: 'There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan', and the guest dropdown options are not visible. No guest range is stated for any venue.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: The legal steps are very clear with official sources ('Gather your documents', 'Submit at least one month before your date', 'Witnesses are optional', sources Justica, IRN, Smartraveller). The advisor will 'help you marry legally for your nationality' and 'We walk you through the exact route', but nothing says they actually prepare or lodge the documents for us.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: 'What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things... We talk you through the options for your plans.' No figure, no 'from' price, no minimum anywhere on the page.

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Catholic marriage is one of three recognised forms and is still registered through the civil registry.' and FAQ 3 'Yes for a Catholic ceremony'.

objections_triggered.objection: Minimum guest numbers or spend that don't fit a small group
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No minimum spend anywhere, plus 'exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill' and the venue cards all at palace or estate scale.
Largely calmed by the numbered legal steps and passport sections; only left open because it says 'talks you through' rather than 'we handle the documents'.

objections_triggered.objection: This is built for big weddings, not close family
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes' (welcome dinner, late party, Sunday brunch) and 'Queluz offers its upper gardens and Throne Room for events'.

trust_signals_noticed: Clear legal steps with official sources named: 'Legal and travel details checked October 2026, with official sources named.'
Passport-by-passport rules with links to US Department of State, GOV.UK, Smartraveller
Nearest airport listed for every region
'Elopements and small weddings are welcome.' (but only at the form)
FAQ 9 says yes to small weddings and elopements
Honest venue caveats like Monserrate roof works and state events cancelling bookings
turn_offs_noticed: Minimums hidden until the call: the cost section gives no number and pushes you to 'Ask us what drives cost'
Most of the page is shown at big scale: palaces, Throne Room, exclusive-use estates, three-day weekend with late party and brunch
Celebrity wedding links (Ronaldo, Perrie Edwards) under Trending

images.stopped_me: quinta-stone-staircase-couple-portugal.jpg ('A quinta staircase before dinner') and registry-table-signing-portugal.jpg, the only ones that look like a couple and the actual signing, which is what I care about.
images.felt_generic: azulejo-tile-wall-detail-portugal.jpg and the fado guitar feel like travel brochure filler. The many palace and terraced vineyard shots repeat (Pena, Monserrate, Douro appear several times each).
images.scale: Almost every image is a venue or landscape. quinta-courtyard-dinner-table and the long quinta dinner suggest a bigger crowd. No image shows a tiny group, just two people, or a family of ten.
images.note: All images are grey placeholders; I reacted to the labels and captions.

emotional_response.overall: Relieved on the legal side, a bit wary on cost and scale.
emotional_response.felt_welcome_as_small_group: Only near the bottom. The top half made me feel like I'd need a palace and 80 guests.
emotional_response.felt_overwhelmed: Somewhat. It is a very long page on my phone and I had to scroll past palaces, settings, vow renewals and birthdays to reach the bits about small weddings.

payload.decision_reason: My two must-haves are just about met: small weddings are clearly welcome (in the form and FAQ 9) and the legal steps are laid out properly with official sources, plus an advisor who helps with my passport route. Catholic is answered. But I'm enquiring partly because the page won't tell me the minimum spend, which I'd rather have seen, and the top half shows everything at palace and three-day-weekend scale, so it is a cautious enquiry, not an excited one.
payload.verbatim_reaction: OK, the legal part is actually really good. I finally get what documents we need and that we don't even need witnesses. And it does say small weddings and elopements are welcome, but I had to scroll right to the form to see it. Up top it's all palaces and Throne Rooms and a weekend with a late party and Sunday brunch, which is not us, it's just our parents and siblings. What I really wanted was a number: what's the minimum? 'Ask us what drives cost' means I have to talk to someone to find out if we're even in range. I'll fill in the form because it's short and I need help with everything, but if the answer is a big minimum I'm out.
